id.description: The question id you were given, echoed back verbatim.

answer.description: Your independently derived answer. Written as if the question had never been answered before, because as far as you are concerned it has not.

grounded_in.description: Every file you actually read to reach this answer, most load-bearing first, as path or path:line. Use the literal string 'prior-knowledge' for any part of the answer you did NOT read from a file in this run — that flag is the single most useful field here, because a prior-knowledge answer is exactly the one most likely to be wrong.

confidence.description: How sure you are of YOUR answer. Low is a legitimate and useful answer.

is_ambiguous.description: True if the question as worded admits more than one defensible answer — for example it does not say which repo, which branch, or whether it means 'written' or 'in effect'.

competing_answers.description: Each defensible reading and what it yields. Empty when is_ambiguous is false.

level.description: stated_verbatim = the answer appears word-for-word somewhere trivially reachable (a code comment, a filename, a doc heading, a commit subject) so any taker can grep it without understanding anything. findable = reachable with one obvious search. none = requires actually reading and reasoning about code.

where.description: Exact locations that give the answer away. Empty when level is none.

checked_for_later_changes.description: Did you actively check whether something LATER overrides the source you answered from — a later migration, a newer commit, current code that diverges from a doc?

notes.description: What you checked and what you found. If an earlier authoritative-looking source disagrees with current reality, say both and say which one you believe.

could_not_verify.description: What you could not establish and why. Naming a gap beats guessing past it.
